items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: But I heard of the band. In fact, I knew the whole band.

ctx.x: I should say he was an original. Jimmy Noon was a great musician. And sure, he had his own sound. Because we copied a lot. Benny Goodman's got a lot of things from Jimmy Noon, a lot of guys. The only guy that played different from all of us, I'll be truthful, was Johnny Dodds. He had something different from all of them. I don't think he's taken any lessons. He learned in another way, but it was so beautiful. This guy played a lot of horn, man. He had his own sound, his own fingering and all. I wonder how he did…
Did you ever hear the original King Oliver Creole jazz band in about 22, 23, with Johnny Dodds and Dewdry at the Lincoln Gardens?

I took Johnny Dodds' place in 24. I knew King Oliver when I was a kid, around New Orleans, playing second trumpet in the brass band with Manuel Perez, an onward brass band. Then I played with King Oliver a couple of times before I went into the Navy, when I was around 16 and 17 years of age. Joe was in his prime then. He'd play these bonkés and things like that and balls. Sure, I knew all the old times, but in 1922, I was in New Orleans. I didn't hear them at the Lincoln Gardens. When we came up there, it was in…
